benefits: $32,650 pa + tuition fees at domestic rate (published award amount on the UC scholarship portal)

Candidates must have completed, or be completing, an appropriate qualifying degree or other qualifications at a level judged equivalent to a bachelor's degree with first-class honours or a master's degree with distinction at UC, with a GPA from the last two years of relevant academic study equivalent to a UC GPA of at least 7.0 (Regulations clause 2.3)
Applicants may not have commenced their doctoral studies at UC more than one year before the closing date for scholarship applications (Regulations clause 2.4)
There are no citizenship or residency requirements for this scholarship (UC scholarship portal fund details)
International students can apply for any UC scholarship unless the regulations specifically restrict it to NZ citizens or holders of NZ residence class visas
requirements: Applications must be made online at the Scholarships website by 11:59 pm (NZT) on 15 May or 15 October (Regulations clause 3.1)
Applicants must have submitted their separate application for admission into the research doctoral degree programme at UC before the scholarship closing date (Regulations clause 2.2)
Most UC scholarships are selected on the basis of the written application and referees' reports; some require an interview with the selection panel
These scholarships are subject to funding availability and are reviewed each year
Late applications are not accepted and the closing date is not flexible
documents: Transcripts or records of learning, including Scholaro reports if previous learning was at an overseas institution
List of referees; referees' reports are a written statement about your abilities from people you nominate, and it is the applicant's responsibility to ensure they arrive by the due date
Proof of citizenship or residency status (for example a birth certificate or passport)
If necessary, an academic or language test
A CV only if it is specifically requested
Privacy provisions that must be signed and dated as part of the application

Project fit with institutional strategic priorities (Regulations clause 5.1d)
Recommendation of the Department/School or delegate (Regulations clause 5.1e)
If in any year there are fewer candidates of sufficient merit than scholarships available, fewer offers are made (Regulations clause 5.2)
coverage: Financial assistance to a value of $32,650 per 120 points + tuition fees for thesis-only enrolment for up to a total of 360 points
In addition to the stipend, the scholarship may also cover tuition fees for thesis enrolment only, at the Aotearoa New Zealand domestic rate (Regulations clause 6.1)

Create a myUC account; UC states you need a myUC account before you can apply for any scholarship

Submit before 11:59pm (NZT) on 15 October, then check the status in 'My Applications' has changed to 'Submitted' and that you received the confirmation email

official.duration: Usually tenable for the period necessary to complete up to 360 points of thesis-only enrolment (about three years of full-time study)

renewal/deferral terms - no statement that the award is renewable or deferrable appears on the pages read

applicant_utility.summary: The UC Doctoral Scholarship pays NZ$32,650 a year plus thesis-only tuition fees at the domestic rate for up to 360 points, and the current round closes 11:59pm NZT on 15 October 2026 for starts before 1 July 2027. Because only thesis tuition is covered, you must fund the Student Services Levy, medical insurance and accommodation yourself - the regulations name all three as not directly covered. Core recipients are also automatically considered for Prestige top-ups of up to $5,000 per 120 points with no separate application. International applicants face no citizenship or residency restriction, but a separate UC doctoral admission application must be lodged before the scholarship closing date.
applicant_utility.best_fit: Graduates with honours-level results (last two years of study equivalent to a UC GPA of 7.0+) entering their first research doctorate at Canterbury, able to start before 1 July 2027.
application_readiness_checklist: Lodge your separate UC doctoral admission application in myUC well before 15 October - the regulations make it a condition of eligibility, not a formality
Convert overseas grades through Scholaro and confirm they meet the UC GPA equivalent of 7.0 over your last two years of relevant study before you apply
Brief referees early on the closing date and what to cover - UC will not chase missing reports and your status sits at 'Request Pending' until they arrive
Re-check that your application status has flipped to 'Submitted' and keep the receipt email; 'Pending Submission' means it never went through
Diarise the fallback May round (opens 20 March, closes 15 May) in case your start date slips past 1 July 2027
common_rejection_risks: No separate UC doctoral admission application submitted before the closing date - a hard exclusion under Regulations clause 2.2
Already holding a doctoral degree, or having started doctoral study at UC more than one year before the closing date - both are outright bars
GPA below the equivalent of UC 7.0 across the last two years of relevant academic study
Referee reports arriving after 15 October; UC states the closing date is not flexible and the Scholarships Office will not follow up missing references
Budgeting as if the stipend covers everything, then arriving without funds for the Student Services Levy, medical insurance and accommodation
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: Student Services Levy, medical insurance and accommodation are explicitly excluded by the regulations, and any living costs beyond the stipend are the student's own responsibility.
document_audit: Overseas study needs Scholaro reports attached, not just raw transcripts
Only include a CV if the application specifically asks for one
The privacy provisions must be signed and dated or the application is incomplete
If a language test is requested it must be arranged in advance - do not leave it to the final week
alerts: The October round is only for doctoral starts before 1 July 2027; a later start puts you in the May round instead
Offers must be accepted or declined within one month of receipt, and enrolment must occur within six months of the offer, or the scholarship is rescinded
The award is subject to funding availability and is reviewed each year, so the published value is not guaranteed for future rounds
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: myUC account -> 'Apply for a Scholarship' -> search UC Doctoral Scholarship -> 'Apply here' -> complete with documents, privacy provisions and referees -> submit before 11:59pm NZT on 15 October -> confirm 'Submitted' status.

official.deadline_note: Three contestable closing dates in 2026 - 1 March, 15 July and 1 November - with applications opening one month before each closing date. AUT advises applying for doctoral admission at least two months before the scholarship round because admissions processing may take up to two months.
official.application_cycle: 2026 contestable rounds closing 1 March, 15 July and 1 November; applications open one month prior to each closing date, so the 1 November round opened on 1 October 2026.
official.status_note: The 1 November 2026 contestable round is open (applications opened 1 October 2026, one month before the closing date).
official.tuition_coverage_note: Published value: 'Tuition fees (at the domestic rate) plus the compulsory student services fee' and 'A stipend of NZ$34,737 per annum for 2026 awards'.
benefits: Tuition fees (at the domestic rate) plus the compulsory student services fee
Part-time study: an annual stipend of $17,368.50 plus tuition fees and the compulsory student services fee for up to six years

Automatic consideration for one of the faculty or school funded options: a full fee scholarship (at the domestic rate), or full fees plus an annual stipend equivalent to at least $20,000 or the minimum living cost criteria for Immigration NZ student visa, whichever is the highest
eligibility: The contestable rounds are open to all eligible applicants - New Zealand citizens or permanent residents, or international students
Applicants must meet the normal admission criteria for the doctoral programme and have received an Offer of Place for the doctoral programme at AUT

Recipients will have an excellent academic record, strong academic references and have demonstrated the potential for high quality research; recipients will normally have the equivalent of first-class honours
Applicants must meet English language proficiency requirements as stated in the Academic Calendar at the time of application
The applicant's proposed field of study must be one where the University can offer supervision; applicants should contact potential supervisors prior to application

Preference will be given to new applicants to the doctoral programme at AUT, including those currently in provisional candidature; for the contestable rounds, grades for the qualifying degree must be available at the time of application, and students awaiting grades must apply in the following round
requirements: It is not possible to submit incomplete scholarship applications through the online application process; incomplete applications will not be forwarded to the selection panel
Two academic reference statements are required for all applicants other than those whose qualifying programme was completed at AUT (AUT applicants provide one referee only)
Applicants must not submit referees' reports directly; nominated referees are sent a request directly from the online application system
The proposal must be two pages only (1,000 words) plus a maximum of one page for any references; longer documents will be asked to be revised
Recipients of stipend scholarships must sign the AUT Postgraduate Scholarship Contract in the portal for any stipend valued at $20,000 or greater
documents: Academic transcript(s) for any tertiary study completed at a university other than AUT
Copy of the conditional or unconditional Offer of Place
Two-page proposal outlining the intended research using the template provided with the online application form (1,000 words plus a maximum of one page of references)
Two academic referees' confidential reports submitted directly to the scholarship portal by the closing date (one referee if the qualifying programme was completed at AUT)
selection_criteria: Particular consideration of the applicant's status with regard to New Zealand citizenship, residency, Maori or Pacific Island ethnicity, and AUT alumni
Demonstrated excellence in the applicant's academic record (including prizes, awards and any publications)
Demonstrated excellence in the applicant's research proposal
The applicant's research and/or professional background and any publication record
Preference is given to applicants who align with the University's strategic plan
coverage: Tuition fees (at the domestic rate) plus the compulsory student services fee
A stipend of NZ$34,737 per annum for 2026 awards
Up to three years of full-time study, or up to six years of part-time study
Stipend paid monthly into the recipient's nominated New Zealand bank account; scholarship payments are not made retrospectively
application_method: Apply for admission into the AUT doctoral programme first - the admissions process may take up to two months, so apply at least two months before the scholarship round
Register on the AUT online scholarships application portal and select which AUT scholarship(s) to apply for

Upload the two-page research proposal (up to 1,000 words plus references), a brief CV (up to three A4 pages), academic transcript(s) for non-AUT tertiary study, and a copy of the conditional or unconditional Offer of Place
Provide details of two academic referees and, via the portal, ask them to submit a confidential report directly to the portal by the closing date
If the proposed AUT primary supervisor or head of school is not one of the referees, provide a letter or evidence of AUT faculty support
Submit the completed application via the portal - this can be done before referees have submitted their reports
official.application_route: Secure an AUT doctoral Offer of Place, then apply via the AUT online scholarships application portal with the research proposal, CV, transcripts, Offer of Place and two referee reports

official.international_eligibility: Yes - open to all applicants including those from countries other than New Zealand who meet the admission requirements for a doctoral programme

applicant_utility.summary: The AUT Doctoral Scholarship pays a NZ$34,737 annual stipend (2026 rate) plus tuition fees at the domestic rate and the compulsory student services fee for up to three years of full-time study, with the current contestable round closing 1 November 2026. You must already hold an Offer of Place for the AUT doctoral programme, and because admissions can take up to two months, admission needs to be lodged well before the scholarship window. The published value contains no travel or research-expense component, so treat the stipend as your living costs. One trap catches offshore applicants: the conditions of acceptance require the scholar to be resident in New Zealand and studying at AUT, and stipends are not paid to students living offshore.
applicant_utility.best_fit: First-class-honours-level researchers, domestic or international, who have secured an AUT doctoral Offer of Place and confirmed AUT supervision for their topic.
application_readiness_checklist: Lodge your AUT doctoral admission at least two months before the round closes; without the Offer of Place you cannot apply at all
Confirm before applying that AUT can supervise your proposed topic - an unsupervised field is ineligible
Cut the research proposal to exactly two pages / 1,000 words plus one page of references using AUT's template, covering topic, rationale, question, method and benefits
Have final qualifying-degree grades in hand at application time; awaiting grades pushes you to the next round
Get both referees to submit through the portal before the closing date and chase them yourself - applications missing reference statements are never released to the panel
common_rejection_risks: Incomplete application - AUT does not forward incomplete applications to the selection panel, full stop
Missing referee statements; the application is considered ineligible without the required references
A proposal over two pages or 1,000 words, which you will be asked to revise
Referee reports supplied by the applicant instead of arriving through the portal system
No evidence of AUT faculty support when neither the proposed supervisor nor head of school is a referee
applicant_utility.estimated_uncovered_costs: The published value is domestic-rate tuition fees, the compulsory student services fee and the stipend only - travel, research expenses and any international-rate fee difference are on you.
document_audit: Transcripts are required only for tertiary study completed at universities other than AUT
A conditional Offer of Place is acceptable - you do not need to have started the programme
Referees receive their request directly from the portal; warn them to watch for the AUT email and note the closing date
alerts: The 2026 rounds close on fixed dates - 1 March, 15 July, 1 November - each opening only one month before closing, so the preparation window is short

Reapplication is limited: shortlisted-but-unsuccessful applicants get one subsequent round only, and unsuccessful-not-shortlisted applicants also get one further attempt and only with a significant change to the application
An AUT Doctoral Scholarship must be taken up within four months of the offer (eight months for international students), and the scholar must be resident in New Zealand while studying at AUT
Co-tenure with other awards is capped at one third of the scholarship value and needs Scholarships Office approval; stipends of $20,000 or more require a signed Postgraduate Scholarship Contract
applicant_utility.submission_workflow: Admission and Offer of Place -> register on the AUT scholarships portal -> upload proposal, CV, transcripts and Offer of Place -> nominate two referees -> submit (referee reports may follow).
